title: This Lizard Shoots Blood From Its Eyes 5 Feet at Anything That Attacks

scenes.text: This lizard shoots blood out of its eyes. Five feet.
The Texas horned lizard. Four inches long. When a coyote grabs it, it fires.
It squeezes shut the veins leaving its head until tiny vessels around the eyelids burst.
A jet of blood flies five feet. Some horned lizards lose a third of their blood doing it.
The blood tastes foul to coyotes. They drop the lizard and shake their heads.
It eats venomous ants all day. That may be why. Five feet.

description:
The Texas horned lizard defends itself by squirting blood from its eyes, up to 1.5 metres (5 feet), at coyotes, foxes and dogs.
It restricts the blood leaving its head until the pressure bursts small vessels around the eyelids. Some horned lizard species lose up to a third of their blood in a single defence. The blood tastes terrible to canids, which drop the lizard; harvester ants make up most of its diet, and their chemicals may be the reason.
Which animal defence would you want? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: IT SHOOTS BLOOD FROM ITS EYES
first_comment: Bonus: the blood trick does nothing against birds, so the lizard puffs itself up to twice its size instead. Would you rather fight a coyote or a hawk?
